full_judgment: 5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint of the suit. Their case, in short, is that the suit is bad for defect of parties and it is also barred by limitation. The suit land was under khash possession of Radha Kishore and he did not give any settlement of this land. Pursuant to the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, the then Government of Pakistan became the owner of the suit land. During the preparation of the S.A. khatian, the suit land was not recorded in the name of the Government because of carelessness and negligence of Survey Department as well as Roads and Highways Department. The suit land was illegally recorded in the names of different persons who are the vendors or transferors of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree as prayed for. On different occasions, Roads and Highways Department requested the plaintiffs to leave the premises but they failed to vacate the premises. On 24.11.2002, the defendants served notices upon the plain-tiffs to show cause as to why they would not be evicted from the suit land. Therefore, the notices were not illegal. For the reasons stated, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
